On Sun, Aug 5, 2012 at 11:18 PM, michael <michael...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello,

I'm wondering if anyone can share an example using Rapache to replace the function of a Perl script in an existing AJAX based web program. In my program, for example, I'd like to replace "perlscript.pl" with some "Rscript.R" as in the following:

function xmlhttpPost(responsestr) {
  var xmlHttpReq;
  xmlHttpReq = new XMLHttpRequest();                  
  xmlHttpReq.open('POST', "http://localhost/cgi-bin/perlscript.pl", true);     
  xmlHttpReq.setRequestHeader('Content-Type', 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded');   
  xmlHttpReq.send(responsestr);
  xmlHttpReq.onreadystatechange = function() {   
    if (xmlHttpReq.readyState == 4) {
      var=(xmlHttpReq.responseText);
    }
  }
};

brew isn't a good option in this case since the rest of my program (which is pretty large) is already developed. I'd love to see an example showing what the JavaScript, apache config, and R files should all look like. My grasp of the concepts described in the documentation is still pretty weak.

Thanks,

Michael

messages.subject: Re: R instead of Perl for AJAX example?
parts:
Thank you. The examples were useful. FYI, if anyone else is looking for a simple example.

1. I took the script from: http://www.degraeve.com/reference/simple-ajax-example.php
2. Replaced "/cgi-bin/simple-ajax-example.cgi" with "/R_scripts/test.R"
3. Created the file "test.R" consisting only of the function "print(POST[[1]])"
4. Added to my apache2.conf file:

<Directory /var/www/R_scripts/>
    SetHandler r-script
    RHandler base::sys.source
</Directory>

Not sure if this is the best example, but it got me started.

messages.subject: Re: R instead of Perl for AJAX example?
parts:
IMO, it's by far better practice not to use brew in R scripts to generate spaghetti code, but to generate JSON, and massage it on the client side afterwards. HTML shouldn't be generated with R, so defer that to the client side, and leave R only to do what it's built for - computation. =)

aL3xa
